questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**I. Complete the sentences below following the instructions in the brackets. (5 marks)**
1. The film was in French. It had subtitles in English so we could understand it. (Link both sentences using a conjunction.)
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Cette partie mobilise cinq transformations grammaticales : la coordination par un connecteur logique de son choix, la structure corrélative "either... or...", le discours indirect interrogatif ("asked if/whether"), la voix passive, et le troisième conditionnel pour exprimer une conséquence hypothétique non réalisée dans le passé.

1. **The film was in French, but it had subtitles in English so we could understand it.** "But" relie les deux idées en marquant la nuance : bien que le film soit en français, les sous-titres ont permis de le comprendre.

rappels_de_methode.competence: Grammaire anglaise : coordination, either...or, discours indirect, passif, 3e conditionnel

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**I. Complete the sentences below following the instructions in the brackets. (5 marks)**
2. I don't know his name. I think it is Peter. My mates say he is John. (Join the second and third sentences using 'either... or...')
questions.corrige_markdown: 2. **I think it is either Peter or John.** "Either... or..." relie les deux hypothèses (celle du locuteur et celle de ses camarades) comme deux possibilités alternatives.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**I. Complete the sentences below following the instructions in the brackets. (5 marks)**
3. Andy asked his sister "Have you consulted a dentist?" (Change this sentence to reported speech.)
questions.corrige_markdown: 3. **Andy asked his sister if/whether she had consulted a dentist.** Une question fermée (oui/non) se rapporte avec "if"/"whether", et le present perfect "have consulted" recule au plus-que-parfait "had consulted".

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**I. Complete the sentences below following the instructions in the brackets. (5 marks)**
4. Cameroon grows good coffee beans. (Change this sentence to the passive voice.)
questions.corrige_markdown: 4. **Good coffee beans are grown in Cameroon.** Le complément d'objet "good coffee beans" devient sujet de la phrase passive ; "by Cameroon" reste également possible mais "in Cameroon" sonne plus naturel pour désigner un pays producteur.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**I. Complete the sentences below following the instructions in the brackets. (5 marks)**
5. Ali went to the airport late. He missed his flight. (Link both sentences using 'if')
questions.corrige_markdown:
5. **If Ali had not gone to the airport late, he would not have missed his flight.** Les deux faits étant déjà accomplis et regrettés, le troisième conditionnel ("if + plus-que-parfait, would have + participe passé") est la structure attendue.

### Piège à éviter
Ne confonds pas le discours indirect d'une question fermée ("if/whether", sans inversion, sujet avant verbe) avec celui d'une question ouverte introduite par un mot interrogatif ("what", "why") : la construction "asked if she had consulted" ne doit jamais garder l'inversion de la question directe.

### Conseil
Pour les phrases de liaison, identifie d'abord la relation logique entre les deux idées (contraste, alternative, condition, cause) avant de choisir le connecteur : cela évite d'utiliser "and" par défaut là où "but" ou "if" serait plus précis.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**II. Complete the following cloze text with expressions chosen from the pairs in the box below. Use each expression once. (5 marks)**

**Box:** Has...been / had...been ; as...as / more...than ; above/inside ; how often/how far ; across/through

Abessolo's sister behaves in a strange way these days. His uncle asked if she (1) ...................... ever ...................... to a psychiatric hospital. Abessolo replied, 'Yes'. His uncle also wanted to know (2) ...................... they consult the psychiatrist. Abessolo said "once every fortnight." Everyone who laid eyes on the girl felt sad. She was (3) ...................... tall ...................... Abessolo with long dark hair. She kept walking for hours with her hands (4) ...................... her head. Most of the younger children in the house were scared of getting too close to her. So they would run into the bedrooms and observe her actions (5) ...................... a window.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Ce texte à trous propose des paires d'expressions dont il faut choisir la bonne moitié selon le contexte : le plus-que-parfait interrogatif indirect ("had...been"), l'adverbe de fréquence interrogatif ("how often"), le comparatif d'égalité ("as...as"), et deux prépositions de position/mouvement ("above", "through").

1. **had...been** — "His uncle asked if she had ever been to a psychiatric hospital." Le discours indirect rapportant une question sur un fait antérieur non daté impose le plus-que-parfait.

**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**II. Complete the following cloze text with expressions chosen from the pairs in the box below. Use each expression once. (5 marks)**

**Box:** Has...been / had...been ; as...as / more...than ; above/inside ; how often/how far ; across/through

Abessolo's sister behaves in a strange way these days. His uncle asked if she (1) ...................... ever ...................... to a psychiatric hospital. Abessolo replied, 'Yes'. His uncle also wanted to know (2) ...................... they consult the psychiatrist. Abessolo said "once every fortnight." Everyone who laid eyes on the girl felt sad. She was (3) ...................... tall ...................... Abessolo with long dark hair. She kept walking for hours with her hands (4) ...................... her head. Most of the younger children in the house were scared of getting too close to her. So they would run into the bedrooms and observe her actions (5) ...................... a window.
questions.corrige_markdown:
5. **through** — "They would run into the bedrooms and observe her actions through a window." "Through a window" décrit le fait d'observer depuis l'intérieur en regardant à travers la vitre.

### Piège à éviter
Dans une paire comme "above/inside", ne choisis pas le mot au hasard : "inside her head" n'aurait aucun sens concret ici, alors que "above her head" décrit un geste corporel visible et cohérent avec le récit.

### Conseil
Lis toujours la phrase complète après avoir rempli le blanc pour vérifier qu'elle produit une image concrète et cohérente : cela permet d'éliminer rapidement l'option de la paire qui ne "se voit" pas dans la scène décrite.
